summary: This RFC adds a way to reset streams in SCTP. Resetting sets a stream's numbering back to zero and tells the application layer, so applications can reuse streams for different purposes without tearing down the association. It builds on SCTP's existing features.

plainLanguage.summary: SCTP numbers the messages on each stream, and those numbers only go up. An application that wants to start a new conversation on a stream it has already used has to live with numbers that carry on from the last conversation. This document adds a way for the two ends of an association to reset those numbers, to reset them together with the association's own numbering, or to ask for more streams, all without closing the connection.

questions: how do you reset an sctp stream
what is the sctp re-config chunk
subtitle: How two SCTP endpoints restart stream numbering, add streams and reset sequence numbers without closing the association.

tldr.problem: Applications using SCTP want to reuse a stream for a new purpose, but the stream's sequence numbers keep counting up, so a new use of an old stream sees message numbers higher than expected.
tldr.mechanism: A new RE-CONFIG chunk carries request and response parameters that reset Stream Sequence Numbers (SSNs) to zero, reset SSNs and Transmission Sequence Numbers (TSNs) together, or add streams, with one request in flight at a time.
tldr.outcome: Endpoints can reset or grow streams on a live association. Support is negotiated at setup, and incoming requests are denied by default in the sockets API until the application enables them.

today: RFC 6525 is a Proposed Standard published in February 2012. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends the SCTP protocol of RFC 4960.

sections.title: Why an Application Wants to Reset a Stream
sections.content:
Many applications that use SCTP want the ability to reset a stream. The intention of resetting a stream is to set the Stream Sequence Numbers of the stream back to zero, with a corresponding notification to the application layer that the reset has been performed. Applications requiring this feature want to reuse streams for different purposes but still use the stream sequence number so that the application can track the message flows. Without this feature, a new use of an old stream would result in message numbers greater than expected, unless there were a protocol mechanism to reset the streams back to zero.

The document also includes methods for resetting the Transmission Sequence Numbers, adding additional streams, and resetting all stream sequence numbers. The SCTP sockets API exposes the sequence numbers used by SCTP for user message transfer, so resetting them can be used by application writers. The corresponding sequence number for TCP is not exposed through the sockets API for TCP.
sections.plainLanguage: Reusing a stream is the point. A stream that carried one conversation cannot be reused cleanly because its message numbers never restart, so the second conversation starts at a number the application does not expect.

sections.title: The RE-CONFIG Chunk
sections.content:
The document adds one new chunk type to SCTP, the Re-configuration Chunk, RE-CONFIG, with chunk type 130. The chunk holds a chunk type, a chunk flags octet that the sender sets to 0 and the receiver ignores, and a chunk length that covers the type, flags and length fields, followed by one or two re-configuration parameters.

The format of the chunk requires that the receiver ignore the chunk if it is not understood and continue processing all the chunks that follow, which is accomplished by the use of the upper bits of the chunk type. All transported integer numbers are in network byte order.

Each RE-CONFIG chunk holds at least one parameter and at most two, and only ten combinations are allowed: an Outgoing SSN Reset Request Parameter; an Incoming SSN Reset Request Parameter; an Outgoing SSN Reset Request together with an Incoming SSN Reset Request; an SSN/TSN Reset Request Parameter; an Add Outgoing Streams Request Parameter; an Add Incoming Streams Request Parameter; an Add Outgoing Streams Request together with an Add Incoming Streams Request; a Re-configuration Response Parameter; a Re-configuration Response together with an Outgoing SSN Reset Request; and two Re-configuration Response parameters. If a sender transmits an unsupported combination, the receiver SHOULD send an ERROR chunk with a Protocol Violation cause.
sections.plainLanguage: All of this travels in one new kind of chunk. It carries at most two parameters, and only in the listed combinations, so both ends know what a chunk can mean. An older endpoint that does not know the chunk simply skips it and carries on with the rest of the message.

sections.title: The Six Parameter Types
sections.content:
Six parameter types are defined for use in the RE-CONFIG chunk. Their formats require that the receiver stop processing the parameter and not process any further parameters within the chunk if the parameter type is not recognized, again through the upper bits of the parameter type. All transported integer numbers are in network byte order.

The Outgoing SSN Reset Request Parameter, type 13, is used by the sender to request the reset of some or all of its outgoing streams. Its length MUST be 16 + 2 * N, where N is the number of stream numbers listed. It carries a re-configuration request sequence number, a re-configuration response sequence number, the sender's last assigned TSN, and the optional stream numbers; if no stream numbers are listed, all streams are to be reset. The re-configuration request sequence number identifies the request and is a monotonically increasing number initialized to the same value as the initial TSN, increased by 1 whenever a new request parameter is sent.

The Incoming SSN Reset Request Parameter, type 14, is used by the sender to request that the peer reset some or all of its outgoing streams. Its length MUST be 8 + 2 * N, and it carries the re-configuration request sequence number and the optional stream numbers.

The SSN/TSN Reset Request Parameter, type 15, is used by the sender to request a reset of the TSN and SSN numbering of all incoming and outgoing streams. Its length MUST be 8, and it carries only the re-configuration request sequence number.

The Re-configuration Response Parameter, type 16, is used by the receiver of a request to respond to it. Its length MUST be 12 if the optional fields are not present and 20 otherwise. It carries the re-configuration response sequence number, copied from the request so that the response can be tied to it, a 4-byte result, and the optional sender's next TSN and receiver's next TSN, which apply only to SSN/TSN reset requests and which must both be present or both absent. The result is one of seven values: 0 for success with nothing to do, 1 for success with the operation performed, 2 for denied, 3 for an error with a wrong SSN, 4 for an error that a request is already in progress, 5 for an error with a bad sequence number, and 6 for in progress.

The Add Outgoing Streams Request Parameter, type 17, is used by the sender to request that an additional number of outgoing streams, which are the receiver's incoming streams, be added to the association. Its length MUST be 12. The Add Incoming Streams Request Parameter, type 18, asks the peer to add additional incoming streams to the association, in the same way and also with a length of 12. The number of new streams is a 2-byte value, and the streams are added in order and are consecutive, so an association with 4 outgoing streams, numbered 0 to 3, that asks for 3 more gets streams 4, 5 and 6. Both parameters end with a reserved field that the sender SHOULD set to 0 and the receiver ignores.
sections.plainLanguage: Six parameters do the work: reset my streams, reset yours, reset everything including the connection's own numbering, ask for more streams in each direction, and answer a request. The answer carries a result code, from nothing to do through performed, denied, and a few error cases.

sections.title: How a Reset Is Carried Out
sections.content:
SCTP streams are uni-directional and there is no correspondence between outgoing and incoming streams. The procedures are designed so that the incoming side always resets its SSN first, before the outgoing side, which means the re-configuration request must always originate from the outgoing side. An endpoint that wants its incoming streams reset must in effect ask the peer to start an outgoing reset procedure and, once that request is acknowledged, let the peer control the reset operation.

Support for the extension is negotiated with the Supported Extensions Parameter of RFC 5061: an endpoint supporting it MUST include the chunk type of the RE-CONFIG chunk in that parameter in either the INIT or the INIT-ACK, and before sending a RE-CONFIG chunk the sender MUST ensure that the peer advertised support. If it did not, the sender MUST NOT send any re-configuration request, and an application request for such service SHOULD be answered with an error saying the peer stack does not support the extension.

At any given time there MUST NOT be more than one request in flight, so if the re-configuration timer is running and the chunk contains at least one request parameter, the chunk MUST be buffered. After sending the chunk, the sender MUST start the re-configuration timer if the chunk contains at least one request parameter, and not otherwise. The timer MUST use the same value as SCTP's data transmission timer, the retransmission timeout, and MUST use exponential backoff, doubling the value at every expiration. If the timer expires, the sender MUST retransmit the chunk, increment the error counts for the association and the destination, and perform threshold management, possibly destroying the association if the retransmission thresholds are exceeded.

When an endpoint wants to reset the SSNs of some or all of its outgoing streams, it sends an Outgoing SSN Reset Request Parameter, provided the re-configuration timer is not running. It MUST stop assigning new SSNs to new user data for the affected streams and queue that data, because it is not known whether the receiver will accept or deny the request, and because a lost request might cause an out-of-sequence error in a stream the receiver is not yet prepared to handle. It then assigns the next re-configuration request sequence number, sets the sender's last assigned TSN to the next TSN it assigns minus 1, and fills in the stream numbers, which SHOULD NOT be present when all outgoing streams are to be reset. Only one SSN/TSN Reset Request SHOULD be sent within 30 seconds.

On the receiving side, the receiver computes a new value for its next TSN and for the peer's next TSN, processes the reset as though a SACK chunk with no gap report and a FWD-TSN chunk with all streams affected had been received, resets the next expected and outgoing SSNs to 0 for all incoming and outgoing streams, and puts a Re-configuration Response Parameter into a RE-CONFIG chunk that is sent after the incoming chunk has been processed completely.

When a request to add streams arrives, the receiver MUST send a response parameter acknowledging or denying the request. If the response is successful the receiver MUST add the requested number of inbound streams, initializing the next expected SSN to 0, and it SHOULD deny the request if the number of streams exceeds a limit that the application should configure.
sections.plainLanguage: Both ends check that the feature is supported at setup, and only one request may be outstanding at a time. The sender stops numbering new messages on the affected streams and holds them until it knows the peer agreed. The receiver resets its numbers, sends its answer, and the sender then lets the held data go with the new numbers.

sections.title: The Sockets API
sections.content:
The section on the sockets API is informational. When the association change notification is delivered and both peers support the extension, SCTP_ASSOC_SUPPORTS_RE_CONFIG should be listed in the sac_info field, and the notification union is extended with three new fields for a stream reset event, an association reset event and a stream change event. These events are delivered when an incoming request was processed successfully or the processing of an outgoing request has finished.

Four socket options are added. SCTP_ENABLE_STREAM_RESET enables or disables stream reset processing, with separate flags for incoming and outgoing reset requests and for the SSN/TSN reset request. SCTP_RESET_STREAMS lets the user request the reset of incoming and/or outgoing streams, with a list of stream identifiers and a count, where a count of zero means the operation is performed on all streams. SCTP_RESET_ASSOC lets a user request the reset of the SSN and TSN, taking the association identifier as its value. SCTP_ADD_STREAMS lets a user request the addition of a number of incoming and/or outgoing streams.

An endpoint can limit the number of incoming and outgoing streams with the sinit_max_instreams field when issuing an SCTP_INIT socket option, and an incoming request asking for more streams than allowed will be denied.
sections.plainLanguage: The application sees three new events, one for a stream reset, one for a full reset and one for a change in the number of streams, and it gets four new socket options to ask for a reset or for more streams. The receiving end can set a limit, and a request beyond the limit is denied.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The SCTP sockets API exposes the sequence numbers of received DATA chunks to the application, and an application might expect them to be monotonically increasing. When the re-configuration extension is used, that might no longer be true, so applications must enable the extension explicitly before it is used, and must subscribe explicitly to the notifications related to the extension before receiving them.

SCTP associations are protected against blind attackers using verification tags, and this is still valid when the re-configuration extension is used, so the extension does not add any additional security risk to SCTP in relation to blind attackers. When both the SSN and the TSN are reset, the maximum segment lifetime is used to avoid TSN wrap-around.
sections.plainLanguage: Because a reset makes the numbers go backwards, an application has to ask for the feature before it sees it. The protection SCTP already has against blind attackers is unchanged, and a full reset respects the maximum segment lifetime so the connection's own numbers cannot wrap around.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content:
IANA has assigned a chunk type for the RE-CONFIG chunk from the pool of chunks with the upper two bits set to 10, and the registration table for the chunk flags of this chunk type is empty. The chunk type 130 is registered as the Re-configuration Chunk, RE-CONFIG.

Six chunk parameter types have been assigned from the pool of parameters with the upper two bits set to 00: 13 for the Outgoing SSN Reset Request Parameter, 14 for the Incoming SSN Reset Request Parameter, 15 for the SSN/TSN Reset Request Parameter, 16 for the Re-configuration Response Parameter, 17 for the Add Outgoing Streams Request Parameter and 18 for the Add Incoming Streams Request Parameter.
sections.plainLanguage: One chunk number and six parameter numbers are registered for the feature.

fields.name: Chunk Flags
fields.desc: Set to 0 by the sender and ignored by the receiver.

fields.desc: Length of the chunk in bytes, including the type, flags and length.

fields.name: Parameter Type
fields.desc: 13 to 18 for the six parameter types.

fields.name: Parameter Length
fields.desc: Length of the parameter in bytes.

fields.name: Re-configuration Request Sequence Number
fields.desc: A monotonically increasing number that identifies the request.

items.label: Outgoing SSN Reset Request
items.desc: Ask the peer to reset some or all of your outgoing streams.

items.label: Incoming SSN Reset Request
items.desc: Ask the peer to reset some or all of its outgoing streams.

items.label: SSN/TSN Reset Request
items.desc: Ask for a reset of the numbering of all incoming and outgoing streams.

items.label: Re-configuration Response
items.desc: The answer to a request, with a result code.

items.label: Add Outgoing Streams Request
items.desc: Ask for more outgoing streams, which are the peer's incoming streams.

items.label: Add Incoming Streams Request
items.desc: Ask the peer to add more incoming streams.

items.desc: The re-configuration sequence number was wrong.
